sections.title: Letter sound acca
paragraphs: The letter name is (acca) /ˈakka/. This written letter has no sound of its own. It is a silent letter, meaning a letter that you write but do not say. You see it in (hotel) /oˈtɛl/, which is a place for travellers to sleep. This letter never makes a sound on its own.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: You make no movement with your mouth for this letter. Keep your lips, tongue and jaw still. Let no breath burst out and do not use your voice. Place a hand on your throat to check. You should feel no puff of air and no shaking before the following sound.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: This letter is always silent on its own. It never makes a sound when it stands at the start of a word. You can see this silent letter in (hanno) /ˈan.no/. Start speaking right away with the vowel that comes next.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not breathe out a puff of air like in the English word hat. Never make a breathy sound deep in your throat. Simply start directly with the next vowel sound, as in the English word honour.
